clue.text: Sticks around, being complacent

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for sticks the other way round

parts.note: to stick is to glue, and gums are glues

explanation.surface: Someone digs in their heels and looks pleased with themselves about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses GUMS (sticks, as a verb: glues).
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a self-satisfied person pleased with their own position.

clue.text: Tempers rising over players making programme

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue, rising means the word for tempers is read from the bottom up

parts.note: fits of temper are strops
the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered actors are turning out a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' signals the reversal, natural in a down entry, and 'over' puts the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportscast is a broadcast of sport, a kind of radio or television programme.

clue.text: One drops in to make one free

indicators.note: in a down entry, the letter for one drops lower down the word, moving one place

parts.note: to make several things one is to unite them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A riddle about a unit falling into place to make a whole.
explanation.walkthrough: In UNITE the I 'drops' one place down the column, giving U-N-T-I-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to release or loosen it, so the verb free fits.

clue.text: A story involving former president's budget

indicators.note: involving means the story wraps around the president's name

parts.note: a fable is a moral story
Gerald Ford was US president in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A tale about an old US president that also deals with the national budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' signals the containment; 'budget' is an adjective here, as in a budget airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, budget means low-cost and cheap, as in budget hotels.

clue.text: Frankfurter perhaps cooked in fat, full-flavoured

parts.note: food cooked in hot fat is fried
rich food is heavy and full-flavoured

explanation.surface: Describes a German sausage sizzled in oil, full of flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frankfurter' looks like the sausage, but it is a person from Frankfurt, who might well be called by this common German first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Frankfurt is German, and this is a typical German man's first name, so it is an example.

clue.text: Keeping fairly quiet, loves husband's sex appeal

indicators.note: keeping means the loves and the husband hold the musical marking between them

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like the letter O, so two loves give two Os
H is the abbreviation for husband
mp, mezzo piano, is the musical marking for moderately quiet

explanation.surface: A wife keeping her voice down while admiring her husband's allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' signals the containment. Love is nil in tennis, and nil looks like the letter O; mp is the musical marking mezzo piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour or attractiveness, often physical allure.

clue.text: Guards object after agent goes up close to duchess

indicators.note: after places the object's word following the reversed agent
in a down clue, goes up means the agent's word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent
an end is an aim or purpose, an object

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of duchess is taken

explanation.surface: Security staff object as a spy climbs close to a duchess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' reverses the agent in this down entry, 'after' orders the pieces, and 'close to duchess' gives its last letter. A fed is a US federal agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard someone or something is to protect it, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Instrument dog found under lake

indicators.note: under in a down entry places the dog's word below the lake's

parts.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
a laika is a Russian hunting dog, also the name of the first dog in orbit

explanation.surface: A dog is discovered beneath the surface of a lake with a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places the dog below the lake in this down entry. Bala (Llyn Tegid) is a lake in north Wales; Laika was the Soviet space dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The balalaika is a Russian stringed instrument with a triangular body.

clue.text: Fair game? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word for game loses its last letter

parts.note: an event is a contest in a sports programme

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a contest was fair and answers that it was not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts the last letter, T, from EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and even both mean balanced, with neither side favoured.

clue.text: Welsh speaker short of time, being one inclined to ramble?

indicators.note: short of means the word for speaker lacks the letter for time

parts.note: a speaker is a talker

explanation.surface: A chatty Welshman who never finishes in time is said to ramble on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' signals the deletion of the letter for time. The pun: to ramble is both to talk aimlessly and to hike.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramble is a country walk, so a rambler is a hiker, a person who walks.

clue.text: Isolation in east of Germany connected with bigotry

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east, the east as named in Germany
racism is bigotry against people of another race

explanation.surface: A report on intolerance leaving people cut off in eastern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in east of Germany' reads as a place but asks for the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism is exclusion from a group, leaving the person shunned and alone.

clue.text: Extract from Parsifal seems wrong

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A critic finds a passage of Wagner's opera Parsifal misjudged.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are at the end of PARSIFAL and the start of SEEMS. Parsifal is Wagner's last opera, which suits the setter's name, Klingsor, its villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false is untrue or incorrect, the adjective sense of wrong.

clue.text: Powerless to stop trend, regularly adapted

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the word for powerless goes inside the other letters
regularly means every other letter of trend is taken, starting with the first

parts.note: something weak lacks power

explanation.surface: Someone is helpless against a fashion and keeps adjusting to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, E, D from tReNd; WEAK goes inside them 'to stop' the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to make small adjustments, so tweaked means altered slightly to fit.

clue.text: Composer, it's said, is a crank

indicators.note: it's said tells us the composer's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: George Frideric Handel composed Messiah

explanation.surface: Someone claims a certain composer is an eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crank' looks like an eccentric person, but here it is the turning lever of a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is a bent arm turned by hand, which is a kind of grip or lever.

clue.text: Yours truly meets a bird in the night — this one?

definitions.text: Yours truly meets a bird in the night — this one?

parts.note: a speaker calling themselves yours truly means me

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the word for night

parts.note: night is the time of darkness, the dark
an owl is a night bird

explanation.surface: The speaker comes across a bird in the dark and asks what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the containment. The whole clue doubles as the definition: the bird met is this songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is a North American songbird, the very bird the speaker meets.

clue.text: Supply son with heroin? A crime, whatever the circumstances

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, supply means bendily, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dealer providing heroin to his son commits a crime, no matter what.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb about dealing but is the adverb from supple: the letters of SON, HEROIN, A CRIME are bent into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless of conditions, as in any weather, wet or sunny.

clue.text: Perhaps Joey is up, alarm having gone off

definitions.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, one example of the class

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Joey has got out of bed because the alarm clock rang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joey' looks like a person's name, but in Australia a joey is a baby kangaroo. 'having gone off' scrambles IS UP ALARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A young kangaroo is carried in a pouch, so it belongs to the pouched mammal group; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Not wanting to get spiteful, Victor ignored meddling

parts.note: if you have gone off something you no longer want it

indicators.note: ignored means the letter for Victor is left out of the word for spiteful

parts.note: vicious means cruel and spiteful
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Victor is ignored by people who would rather not be nasty about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' signals the deletion of V, Victor in the NATO alphabet; going off something means no longer wanting it.
explanation.definitionFit: An officious person interferes and asserts authority where it is not wanted.

clue.text: Vocal passage, alternatively in F minor, is easy

indicators.note: vocal signals that the passage's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a strait is a narrow sea passage

indicators.note: in places the word for alternatively inside F and the word for minor

parts.note: a ward is a minor in the care of a guardian
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A sung passage that can also be played in the key of F minor is simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal passage' looks musical; 'Vocal' marks a sea passage heard aloud, and 'in' signals the containment. A ward is a minor in care.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple and uncomplicated is plain and easy to do or understand.

clue.text: Passionate anger when Catholic becomes Protestant finally

indicators.note: becomes says one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: to incense is to anger

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of Protestant is used

explanation.surface: Fury erupts when a Catholic converts to Protestantism in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' swaps C in INCENSE for T, the last letter of Protestant.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and ardent, like passionate ones.

clue.text: Apple runs America, agreed?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
US is the United States of America
something agreed is set, as in a set price

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tech company called Apple controls America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple' suggests the computer firm, but it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a variety of apple with rough brownish skin.

clue.text: Beginning to murmur, speak?

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of murmur is taken

parts.note: to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: Someone starts mumbling and is asked if that counts as speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: M, from 'Beginning to murmur', plus UTTER; the whole clue also defines the answer, speaking in a low murmur.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to speak quietly and indistinctly, a murmur of words.

clue.text: Old bailiff delivers flyer

definitions.meaning: a medieval officer who managed a manor or district for a lord
the female of the ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: A manor official from long ago hands out leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a medieval manor official and a female ruff, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Remains with company in outskirts of Cracow, a money-spinner

indicators.note: in puts the remains and the company between those outer letters
outskirts of means only the outer letters of Cracow are used

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A business set up on the edge of a Polish city to deal in remains makes money.
explanation.walkthrough: ASH and CO go 'in' C and W, the 'outskirts of Cracow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably generates profit.

clue.text: Warm wind not OK for this fabric

indicators.note: not means the letters OK are taken out of the wind's name

parts.note: the chinook is a warm dry wind off the Rocky Mountains

explanation.surface: A warm breeze is no good for a particular kind of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not OK' removes OK from CHINOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton cloth used for trousers.

clue.text: Team from NW town missing the final

indicators.note: missing the final means the last letter of the town is dropped

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, in north-west England

explanation.surface: A northern football side failed to reach the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the final' drops E from CREWE, a railway town in Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group working together, such as a boat's rowers or a ship's company.

clue.text: Government's in control, as a rule

indicators.note: in puts the letter for government inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a tight rein
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: The government is usually in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Government' looks like the definition, but it supplies G, which goes 'in' REIN; 'as a' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is their rule, the period or exercise of sovereign power.

clue.text: Assorted secret items and objects, primarily?

definitions.text: Assorted secret items and objects, primarily?

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order
primarily means the first letters of items, and, objects are taken

explanation.surface: A description of a mixed collection of hidden things and objects.
explanation.walkthrough: SECRET plus I, A, O ('primarily') are 'Assorted'. The whole clue also defines the answer: obscure items known only to a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are things understood by only a select few, so secret items fits.

clue.text: Insect devoured by extremely savage creature

indicators.note: devoured by means the insect ends up inside the other word

parts.note: wildest is the superlative of wild, so most savage
a bee is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug is eaten by a really fierce beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoured by' signals the containment; 'extremely' makes the superlative, not an outer-letters pick.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is a large African antelope, an animal.

clue.text: Guy needs something to wear, first off

indicators.note: first off means the first letter of the garment is removed

parts.note: a smock is a loose garment

explanation.surface: A man needs some clothing before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is the verb meaning to ridicule. 'first off' removes S from SMOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to make fun of them, a synonym of the verb meaning ridicule.
